semantic_correction.stem: A nurse is caring for an adult client with a tracheostomy in an acute-care unit. Which emergency equipment set should be immediately available in the room?

options.A: A replacement tracheostomy tube, obturator, bag-valve-mask device, and suction catheter kit.
options.B: A pulse oximeter, stethoscope, incentive spirometer, and oral airway.
options.C: A spare tracheostomy tie set, dressing kit, oxygen tubing, and nebulizer mask.
options.D: A chest-drainage kit, oral suction tip, nasal cannula, and blood-pressure cuff.

semantic_correction.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills states that a replacement tracheostomy tube, an obturator, a bag-valve-mask device, and a suction catheter kit must be available in the room for patient safety. The same chapter also notes that acute-care bedside equipment should include spare tracheostomy tubes, including the same size and one size smaller, and a bag-valve-mask device. The other equipment sets may contain useful monitoring or routine-care items but do not provide the complete airway-rescue capability described by the source.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Maintain immediate access to essential tracheostomy airway-rescue equipment: replacement tracheostomy tube, obturator, bag-valve-mask device, and suction setup.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor pattern, shortened the correct equipment bundle, and rebuilt all alternatives as parallel four-item bedside equipment sets so the answer depends on airway-rescue function rather than wording cues.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Nursing Skills Chapter 22 — bedside safety equipment and tracheostomy suctioning safety note
audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was correct but distractors were uneven. The revised item uses four parallel equipment bundles and preserves the exact source-supported rescue equipment set.

option_audit.A: Correct. All four components are explicitly identified by NCBI Nursing Skills as in-room tracheostomy safety equipment.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Monitoring and respiratory-support items do not replace the replacement tube, obturator, BVM, and suction equipment needed for airway rescue.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Routine tracheostomy-care supplies do not provide the complete emergency airway-rescue set.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. These items are not the tracheostomy-specific emergency equipment set identified in the source.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A is the only option containing the complete source-defined emergency tracheostomy equipment set.
cueing_check: All four choices are four-item bedside equipment bundles of comparable length and syntax; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
